To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extinction coefficients and oscillator strength of the first strong triplet-triplet transitions in naphthalenes, phenanthrenes, and triphenylenes were measured and found to be 14000 liter/mole· cm, 0.05, 27000 liter/mole ·cm, 0.11, 7000 liter/mol·cm, 0,05, respectively.
The extinction coefficient and oscillator strength of the first strong triplet-triplet transition of naphthalene is emax=14,000 liter/mole⋅cm, and f=0.050.

the extinction coefficients of the lowest-energy triplet–triplet transition in the three polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons studied were found to be 14 000, 27 000, and 7 000 L mol–1 cm–1, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the photophysics and photochemistry of polynuclear aromatic compounds.
the study of the electronic states of aromatic hydrocarbons in the solid state.

the study of the electronic structure of aromatic molecules in the excited singlet and triplet states, and of the interaction between the excited molecules and the solvent molecules in the ground state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the extinction coefficients of the first strong triplet--triplet transition in aromatic molecules are of the order 10 4 liter/mole· cm, and the oscillator strengths of these transitions are of the order of 10 -2.

the extinction coefficient and oscillator strength for the first strong transition in a given molecule are approximately proportional to the number of benzene rings in the molecule, with an additional factor of 3 for a triphenylene ring.
the extinction coefficients of the triplet-triplet transitions in aromatic molecules are in the range from 10 000 to 30 000 liter/mode·cm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oscillator strength of the first strong triplet→triplet transition is 0.03-0.04 in aromatic compounds.
the extinction coefficients for the first allowed transitions in the aromatic hydrocarbons are about 10 000 liter/mode·cm, and the oscillator strengths are about 0.04.
the extinction coefficients for the first triplet↔tripplet transition in polynuclear hydrocarbons are about 10 000 to 20 000 liter/mode·cm and the oscillator strength is about 0.10.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extinction coefficient of a triplet-triplet transition is not necessarily small and can be comparable to that of a singlet-singlet transition.
the oscillator strengths for the first triplet--triplet transition are small, and that the extinction coefficients for this transition are large.
the extinction coefficients of triplet↔triplets transitions in aromatic compounds are much larger than the extinction coefficients of singlet↔triplets and singlet↔singlets.
